convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in indicators (iSAR, iADX) and simple market orders, but includes MQL5 Trade Standard Library .mqh includes (Trade.mqh, SymbolInfo.mqh, DealInfo.mqh, PositionInfo.mqh) and MT5-specific position/deal history logic (CheckAllowedDir) that requires manual Python reimplementation. No grid/martingale, but deal-history-based direction filter is non-trivial.

derived_values.name: ADir - last deal direction bias
derived_values.formula: Scans deal history for most recent closing deal on symbol; if profitable sell → aDir=1 (favor buys), if profitable buy → aDir=-1 (favor sells); if losing, reverses the bias
derived_values.used_by: entry rule - gates trade direction based on last closed deal outcome

derived_values.formula: iSAR(_Symbol, PERIOD_CURRENT, SARStep, SARMax) buffer 0 at bar Shift

derived_values.name: a0 - ADX main value at Shift bar
derived_values.formula: iADX(_Symbol, PERIOD_CURRENT, ADXPeriod) buffer 0 at bar Shift

derived_values.name: cl0 - Close price at Shift bar

other_exits: BreakEven: when position profit >= BreakEven points (50), SL is moved to entry price (breakeven level). For BUY: if current SL < open price and Bid - Point*BreakEven >= open price, move SL to open price. For SELL: if current SL > open price and Ask + Point*BreakEven <= open price, move SL to open price. Respects broker StopsLevel minimum distance.

params.formula_when_lots_zero: FreeMargin * MaximumRisk / 1000.0, then normalized to volume step/min/max

position_sizing.conditional_logic: if Lots input == 0, use deposit_fraction sizing; otherwise use fixed Lots value

custom_logic_notes: CheckAllowedDir implements a deal-history-based direction filter: scans all historical closing deals for the symbol, finds the most recent, and sets aDir based on whether it was profitable. Profitable sell → favor buys (aDir=1), profitable buy → favor sells (aDir=-1). Losing deals reverse the bias. This acts as a rudimentary 'last trade outcome' bias filter. The BreakEven function only moves SL to entry price (not a full trailing stop). The ADX buffer 0 (main ADX line) is used, not the +DI/-DI buffers, so the condition checks overall trend strength being below the threshold (ranging market filter).
python_conversion_notes: Entry logic is straightforward: Close > SAR AND ADX < 20 for longs; Close < SAR AND ADX < 20 for shorts. The CheckAllowedDir function requires maintaining a trade history log in the Python backtest to replicate the last-deal-outcome direction bias. BreakEven logic is simple SL-to-entry move once profit threshold reached. Position sizing has two modes: fixed lots or free-margin-based calculation. The SAR and ADX indicators are available in pandas-ta/ta-lib. Key nuance: ADX buffer 0 is the main ADX line (not +DI/-DI), so use adx() not adx_pos/adx_neg. The deviation/spread logic for order execution can be simplified in backtest.
